title: Run four coding agents on one shared machine around the clock
summary: A founder open-sourced Aisevak, where Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Devin share one server, hand off tasks and open new ones; he says much of Embedr runs on it.
agent_role: A lead agent splits tasks and hands them to builder and reviewer agents, each in its own copy of the code. People assign tasks and steer through a web app.
outcome: The author says a lot of his company Embedr now runs on it.
what_they_did: The developer built a self-hosted workspace where several coding agents run 24/7 on one server. A lead agent breaks tasks down and assigns them to other agents. Each works in its own copy of the code. They message each other through a shared command tool, and can run scheduled jobs and log incidents.
how_it_went: The author says a lot of his company Embedr runs on it, and he has now open-sourced it.
worth_knowing: It ships with a safety mode that only records unsafe or duplicate work at first. The readme suggests switching to blocking it once the logs look right.
prompt: Help me set up Aisevak from [repo URL] on [my server]. Walk me through installing it, then connect [Codex / Claude Code / other agent] with my own account. Create two agents: a Builder and a Reviewer, with prompts describing their jobs. Then add my repository [repo] and create a first task: [small task]. Have the Builder do it in its own copy of the code and the Reviewer check it. Show me the final changes and wait for my approval before merging anything.

curation.rationale: Open-source setup where Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Devin share one machine and hand work to each other, which the author says runs much of their company. Mostly a feature description with little concrete outcome.
